description: We are a team of AI and full-stack developers building an autonomous deep-space bio-telemetry and AI triage cockpit for the Astronaut Health Monitoring challenge. Our stack includes Python, GenAI/agentic workflows, NASA API integration, and high-contrast modern web UI. Join us if you want to ship a polished, functional prototype built to win Global Awards. Looking for teammates skilled in frontend/3D UI, Python/data engineering, or pitch deck & video storytelling!
summary:
We developed ASTRA-CDSS, an AI-assisted Clinical Decision Support System designed to monitor astronaut health and support medical decision-making during space missions. The platform features a centralized health dashboard with vital-sign monitoring, health history, interactive data visualizations, alerts, and AI-assisted health risk assessment. It aims to help track astronaut health conditions and identify potential medical concerns.
Space missions expose astronauts to challenging conditions such as microgravity, isolation, and limited access to immediate medical facilities. ASTRA-CDSS addresses these challenges by bringing essential health information into a single platform. It provides continuous health-status visualization, organizes medical history, highlights potential health risks, and generates alerts to support faster and more informed medical decisions, especially when communication with Earth is limited.
Astronaut health and safety are critical to the success of every space mission. Medical emergencies in space can be difficult to manage because of limited resources and delayed communication with Earth. ASTRA-CDSS aims to improve early risk identification, support timely medical decisions, and reduce dependence on Earth-based medical assistance. Beyond space exploration, its approach could also inspire intelligent remote healthcare monitoring systems for people in isolated and resource-limited environments.
details:
ASTRA-CDSS — Project Description

1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

ASTRA-CDSS (Astronaut Self-Health Tracking and Clinical Decision Support System) is an AI-assisted health monitoring and clinical decision support prototype designed to support astronaut health during space missions. It provides a centralized dashboard to monitor vital signs, review medical history, visualize health trends and identify potential health risks.

The system organizes health information into an accessible interface. Vital-sign readings can be reviewed through visual charts, while alerts highlight potentially concerning values. Its AI-assisted risk assessment component is intended to support early identification of potential health concerns and more informed decision-making.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Improves astronaut health awareness through centralized monitoring.
  • Helps highlight potentially concerning health readings.
  • Organizes vital signs, medical history and alerts in one interface.
  • Uses charts to make health trends easier to understand.
  • Supports health-related decision-making.
  • Provides a concept for remote health monitoring in isolated environments.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact of ASTRA-CDSS is to improve astronaut health awareness and support safer decision-making during long-duration space missions. By combining health information, monitoring and risk alerts, the system aims to help identify potential medical concerns earlier and support timely responses.

The concept could also inspire remote health-monitoring applications on Earth, including research stations, disaster-response locations and communities with limited access to healthcare.

4. What tools did you use?

The project was developed using React.js, JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Tailwind CSS. Recharts was used for data visualization, and Vercel was used for hosting and deployment. AI-assisted development tools supported the development process.

5. How is your project creative?

ASTRA-CDSS creatively combines astronaut health monitoring, data visualization and AI-assisted clinical decision support in a single interface. Rather than displaying disconnected health readings, it organizes vital signs, medical history, trends and alerts into a centralized dashboard.

Its innovation lies in adapting a digital health-monitoring concept to the challenges of space exploration, where astronauts operate in isolated environments and immediate access to Earth-based medical care may be limited.

6. What factors did your team consider, such as energy, accessibility or cost?

Our team considered several practical factors:

  • Energy: A lightweight web application can reduce unnecessary processing and resource usage.
  • Accessibility: We prioritized a clear, readable and responsive interface with understandable charts and health information.
  • Cost: We used accessible web technologies and online hosting to develop the prototype without expensive specialized hardware.
  • Reliability: We designed the interface to make health readings and potential warning conditions easy to identify.
  • Privacy: Future versions should include secure storage, encryption and controlled access to sensitive health information.
  • Space constraints: Future development should consider limited connectivity, onboard computing resources and offline operation.

These considerations guided our prototype design. Further testing and development would be required before real-world spaceflight use.
